page: Microsoft Azure D16s_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. The system provides 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores via hyperthreading, paired with 64 GB of total system RAM, adhering to a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio (4 GB per vCPU). The CPU architecture includes 260 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and advanced vector capabilities including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX).

The virtual machine does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, functioning instead with remote persistent block storage through Azure Premium Storage support. Benchmark evaluations position the instance firmly in the middle 50% across general computing, multi-core processing, and memory bandwidth, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 11,424 and a PassMark CPU score of 26,651.67. Performance elevates into the top 25% bracket for text processing tasks and lightweight language model generation using compact architectures.

Without local NVMe drives to offset operational overhead, resource efficiency depends on sustained utilization of its dedicated compute threads and AMX matrix capabilities. The balanced ratio of compute to memory makes Microsoft Azure D16s_v6 suitable for web application hosting, Redis caching tiers, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and transactional enterprise databases.
description: Microsoft Azure D16s_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture using an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The instance delivers 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, alongside 64 GB of memory maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Dedicated hardware extensions include AVX-512, AMX tile, and AMX int8 instructions. The server includes no onboard local storage, depending entirely on remote premium storage attachments, and contains no graphical processing units. Benchmark measurements show steady median-tier compute and memory throughput, alongside strong results in text processing and small-model language generation. With a solid memory allocation and robust vector acceleration, this instance is suited for multi-tier web serving, software compilation, database tasks, and in-memory key-value caching workloads such as Redis.
